title: The Revolving Sushi Mystery
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Professor Agasa, Ai/Haibara, Ayumi, Genta, Mitsuhiko, Detective Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Only 4 named case-specific persons appear in the transcript (victim + 3 suspects); the victim's wife is referenced but never named, so she gets no node. The old lower-fidelity case file's stated culprit (Osamu Aizono) is CONFIRMED correct against the transcript -- no culprit discrepancy. However the old file's clue c1/e1 description ('Agatsuma publicly humiliated Aizono ... correcting his sushi identification') understates what actually happened: the transcript reveals Agatsuma didn't just correct Aizono, he deliberately SWITCHED the sea bass and flounder plates beforehand to engineer Aizono's public embarrassment in front of his wife, then followed up with a sustained campaign of harassment on Aizono's food blog -- a premeditated targeting, not an honest correction, which better explains the intensity of Aizono's motive (his wife later divorced him partly over the fallout). The old file also omits the two other suspects' backstory motives (Takemura's shop closure, Namiki's career-ending wrist injury) captured here as red-herring has_motive_against edges, and omits the restaurant manager Namiki and customer Takemura almost entirely as narrative figures. Location name 'Sushi shop Senpuken' is carried over from the old file/wiki since it is not stated in the read transcript excerpt (flagged in the location's attrs). case_type: murder. Per the temporal-fields policy (2026-08, batch 8+), order/temporal_frame/years_before_present are omitted from all edges.

clues.desc: Victim was left-handed and always set his used wipe down on his left -- only the seat to his immediate left (Aizono's) could plant a swapped wipe there.
No hand wipe remained at the victim's seat, yet a torn corner of a wipe packet did -- shows the poisoned wipe+packet were deliberately removed, not simply used up.
